children: Ciena lifted its revenue guidance after reporting a more-than-fivefold increase in its third-quarter profit, driven by networking demand tied to artificial-intelligence investments.
The networking-systems and software company said it now expects full-year revenue of $6.37 billion to $6.47 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet currently expect $6.34 billion.

The lift to guidance comes as Ciena on Thursday logged a profit of $266.4 million, or $1.83 a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 1. That compares with a profit of $50.3 million, or 35 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, the company reported adjusted earnings of $2.11 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting $1.73 a share.
Revenue rose 37% to $1.67 billion, beating the $1.64 billion analysts had been expecting.

The company's most lucrative segment, networking platforms, reported $1.36 billion in sales, up from $941.4 million a year prior. Ciena's global-services unit reported revenue rising to $193.6 million from $160.2 million.

"Today's outstanding financial performance demonstrates Ciena's leadership in providing industry-leading, high-speed connectivity solutions as AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment," Chief Executive Officer Gary Smith said.
For the current fourth quarter, the company expects revenue between $1.7 billion and $1.8 billion. Analysts are expecting $1.7 billion.
Shares of Ciena were down 3.3% at $342.42 in pre-market trading on Thursday.
